title: Attempt on Randomized tree automata and endogeny
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Randomized tree automata and endogeny structural argument Result: Let each vertex state be its own independent Bernoulli(p) innovation, ignoring its children. The pivot tree is empty and the state is measurable from the marked tree, but for 0<p<1 it is independent of the unmarked tree and cannot be a measurable function of that tree. Check: Conditional variance given the bare tree is p(1-p)>0; conditional variance given innovations is0. Obstruction: A literal extension retaining only the unmarked-tree sigma-field is false. A useful theorem must specify the innovation sigma-field and then handle nontrivial child dependence.

title: Attempt on Server provisioning for a finite response-time SLO
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: For the stable M/M/k FCFS benchmark with total arrival rate Lambda and service rate mu per server, let C be Erlang-C and a=k*mu-Lambda. Waiting time is zero with probability 1-C and otherwise Exp(a), independent of the tagged Exp(mu) service. For a!=mu this gives P(T>t)=(1-C)*exp(-mu*t)+C*[mu*exp(-a*t)-a*exp(-mu*t)]/(mu-a). At a=mu the bracket is exp(-mu*t)*(1+mu*t). This gives a reproducible benchmark for each k; simply using the waiting-time tail as the response-time tail would omit service. Check: Convolve the two exponential distributions, and take the continuous limit a->mu to obtain the Erlang-two tail. At t=0 the expression equals one, and at C=0 it reduces to the service tail. Obstruction: The benchmark neither proves the minimum k over all policies nor transfers to M/G/k. No new general staffing rule is established.

title: Attempt on Brownian SIR survival in dimensions at least two
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Counterexample to the usual pathwise lifetime monotonicity coupling Result: Consider a deterministic contact schedule with A initially infected: A-C at time .1, A-B at 1, C-B at 9, B-D at 10, and no other contacts. Baseline infectious lifetimes are L_A=.5, L_C=12, L_B=2. Then B is infected at 9 and infects D at 10. Multiply every lifetime by 3: A now infects B at 1; B is removed at 7, cannot be reinfected at 9, and D is never infected. Check: Check both timelines: C remains infectious at 9 in each case; A has already died at 1 only in the baseline. The example refutes infection-set inclusion under scaled lifetimes on a fixed contact schedule. Obstruction: This is not a counterexample to survival monotonicity or to the Brownian epidemic conjecture. It blocks a direct attractiveness proof; a Brownian contact-support realization was not proved.

title: Attempt on BK disjoint occurrence for weighted uniform spanning trees
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: BK for fixed conjunctions and a nonincreasing-event obstruction Result: For disjoint fixed edge sets F and H, the spanning-tree determinantal formula and Hadamard-Fischer inequality give P(F union H subset T)<=P(F subset T)P(H subset T). Thus fixed increasing conjunctions obey the desired inequality. The increasing condition matters: on a triangle, A={e in T} and B={f not in T}, e!=f, have disjoint coordinate witnesses but P(A intersection B)=1/3>2/9=P(A)P(B). Check: There are three equiprobable spanning trees of a triangle, which checks the latter probabilities directly. The determinantal argument is for a positive semidefinite transfer-current kernel. Obstruction: General increasing disjoint occurrence is a union over adaptive witnesses. A fixed-coordinate negative-association inequality cannot simply be applied after that union.

title: Attempt on Intrinsic-distance two-point function asymptotics in high dimensions
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Relate the intrinsic distance to the number of pivotals along the backbone plus the sizes of the intermediate sausages. Result: The intrinsic distance from 0 to x equals the sum over the backbone decomposition of the intrinsic distances through each 'sausage' between consecutive pivotal bonds; the number of pivotals is the object of Theorem 15.4, and the sausage lengths are i.i.d.-like with a fixed law in the mean-field picture (each sausage is a doubly connected piece of bounded expected size in d > 6 with exponential tails?). If the sausage intrinsic lengths were i.i.d. with finite mean m, then d(0,x) ~ m times the number of pivotals, and the intrinsic two-point function would follow from Theorem 15.4 by a renewal argument with n replaced by n/m. The obstruction is the dependence between sausage sizes and the backbone geometry, which is weak in high dimensions but not zero; the lace expansion with a memory of the intrinsic length would need a new expansion variable (a generating function in both the spatial variable and the intrinsic length), which is what the source suggests. A rigorous partial result: the intrinsic length is at least the number of pivotals plus one, so tau_n^{(in)} summed over n >= N is bounded by the pivotal-count two-point function summed over counts >= N... wait the direction: d(0,x) >= |Piv(0,x)| + 1 gives P(d >= N) >= P(|Piv| >= N - 1), a lower bound on the intrinsic tail from the pivotal tail, hence the intrinsic one-arm probability is at least the pivotal one-arm probability, consistent with both being of order 1/N. No asymptotic constant. Key identity: d_{C(0)}(0,x) >= |Piv(0,x)| + 1, so intrinsic tails dominate pivotal tails. Obstruction: Joint expansion in space and intrinsic length not available.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0079-intrinsic-distance-two-point-function-asymptotics-in-high-dimensions

title: Open problem: Chaos implies multiple peaks without nonnegative correlations
body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Show that chaos implies the multiple-peaks property for Gaussian fields whose correlations are not all nonnegative, which requires a second-moment bound on the overlap R(I_0, I_t) between the maximiser at time 0 and at time t. Source: Chatterjee: Chaos, concentration and multiple valleys, 2008, with open questions, Section 12, problem (5), p. 59.
Posed in Chatterjee: Chaos, concentration and multiple valleys, 2008, with open questions
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

title: Attempt on Chaos implies multiple peaks without nonnegative correlations
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Attempt the second-moment bound on the overlap via Gaussian interpolation. Result: In the nonnegatively correlated case the source bounds E[R(I_0,I_t)^2] using FKG-type positivity; in general the overlap between the argmax at time 0 and at time t is a function of the field and its noised copy, and its second moment can be written through the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup: E[R(I_0,I_t)^2] = E[R(I_0,I_t)] + Var-type terms involving four copies of the field (two pairs). The needed inequality is E[R^2] <= C (E R)^2 + o(1), a 'concentration of the overlap' statement; without positivity one can attempt Gaussian interpolation between the four-copy system and an independent system, whose derivative is a sum of covariance terms of mixed sign, which is exactly where positivity was used. A weaker statement is available: chaos (E R(I_0,I_t) -> 0) gives, by Markov, P(R > delta) -> 0, and multiple peaks in the WEAK sense (existence of a near-maximiser with small overlap) follows from that with the near-maximum condition replaced by the maximum of the noised field, which is a near-maximum of the original field with deficit of order sqrt(t) times the field's variance scale; so 'chaos implies multiple peaks' holds in the sense where the deficit delta_n is of order sqrt(t_n) sigma_n for the chaos time scale t_n, without any second-moment bound; the source's stronger version with the deficit o(m_n)... this weak version I can defend; the second-moment strengthening remains open. Key identity: Noised-field maximiser is a near-maximiser of the original field with deficit O(sqrt(t) sigma_n); chaos gives small overlap in probability, hence weak multiple peaks without positivity. Obstruction: Second moment of the overlap without positive correlations.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0122-chaos-implies-multiple-peaks-without-nonnegative-correlations
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

title: Attempt on Almost-sure convergence in the heavy-tailed circular law
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Borel-Cantelli over the Hermitisation: identify which estimate is only in probability. Result: The proof of Theorem 6.2 has three inputs: (i) convergence of the singular-value distributions of n^{-1/alpha}X - z for each z, which is almost sure by the objective method (the local weak convergence to the PWIT holds a.s.); (ii) uniform integrability of log at infinity, a.s. from moment bounds; (iii) uniform integrability of log near zero, i.e. a lower bound on the small singular values, which is where only an in-probability bound s_n(n^{-1/alpha}X - z) >= n^{-c} with probability 1 - o(1) is available. To make (iii) almost sure one needs the failure probability summable in n, i.e. a bound like P(s_n <= n^{-c}) <= n^{-1-eps}. For heavy tails the row norms are not concentrated and the Rudelson-Vershynin small-ball argument gives only polynomial failure probabilities with exponent that is not obviously above 1. If the failure probability were shown to be O(n^{-1-eps}) (for instance via an Esseen-type anti-concentration in the alpha-stable domain, which gives exponent depending on alpha), Borel-Cantelli finishes the a.s. statement. So the problem reduces to a quantitative smallest-singular-value bound for heavy-tailed matrices with summable failure probability; the bound is plausible but I did not prove it. Obstruction: Need P(s_n(n^{-1/alpha}X - z) <= n^{-c}) summable in n for heavy-tailed entries.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0031-almost-sure-convergence-in-the-heavy-tailed-circular-law

title: Attempt on Ballisticity criterion under the positivity assumption instead of bounded stacks
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check the branching-process-with-migration proof for its dependence on bounded stacks. Result: Under (BD) the branching process with migration has bounded migration per generation, and the criterion delta > 2 comes from the tail of the total progeny of a critical branching process with migration delta: P(total progeny > n) ≍ n^{-delta/2}... the speed is positive iff the expected total progeny (expected excursion time) is finite iff delta > 2. With unbounded stacks under (POS1) the migration is unbounded but positive; the total progeny tail is then governed by the same exponent if the migration has finite mean, and the natural conjecture is that the criterion persists as long as the expected total drift delta = E sum_i (2 omega(0,i) - 1) is finite, with additional conditions on the tail of the stack size (as in the source's assumption (6.2) with the exponential-moment-type condition on the number of cookies far from 1/2). A partial result: under (POS1), (IID), (UEL) and E[sup{i : omega(0,i) not 1/2}] < infinity (the condition in (6.2)), the branching process with migration has migration with finite mean, and the Kesten-Kozlov-Spitzer-type tail analysis for branching processes with migration of finite mean gives the same exponent delta/2 for the total progeny, hence the same criterion delta > 2 for positive speed; the source proves the recurrence/transience part under (6.2) for the functional CLT in the recurrent regime, so the ballisticity part appears to follow the same route. I did not verify the tail analysis under unbounded migration with finite mean; recorded as the expected answer with the condition from (6.2). Key identity: Total progeny tail exponent delta/2 depends on the mean migration, not on its boundedness, if the migration has finite mean. Obstruction: Tail analysis of branching with unbounded finite-mean migration not verified.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0134-ballisticity-criterion-under-the-positivity-assumption-instead-of-boun

title: Open problem: Absolutely continuous invariant measure for the environment seen from the particle versus ballisticity
body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For a RWRE satisfying (ERG) and (E) and transient in a direction, is the existence of an invariant probability measure for the environmental process absolutely continuous with respect to P equivalent to ballisticity in that direction? Source: Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment, Open question 2.19, p. 24.
Posed in Drewitz and Ramirez: Selected topics in random walks in random environment
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

title: Attempt on Absolutely continuous invariant measure for the environment seen from the particle versus ballisticity
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check both implications through the ergodic theorem for the environment process. Result: One direction is standard: if an invariant absolutely continuous probability measure Q exists and is ergodic, the ergodic theorem for the environment chain gives X_n/n -> E_Q[local drift] a.s., and transience in direction l plus Kozlov's theorem (Q equivalent to P, unique) makes the limit velocity well defined; it is nonzero in direction l provided E_Q[d(0,omega) . l] > 0, which follows from transience in direction l ONLY IF one also knows the velocity cannot vanish under transience, which is itself the ballisticity question, so this direction reduces to: invariant a.c. measure + transient in l implies v . l > 0. Under (E) the Kalikow-type argument gives v . l >= 0 but not strict positivity. The converse (ballistic implies invariant a.c. measure) is known under (UE) and (IID) from the renewal structure with finite expected regeneration time; under (ERG) only, regenerations are unavailable and the construction of Q fails. Both directions therefore reduce to statements known under (IID)+(UE) and unproved under (ERG)+(E). Obstruction: Without i.i.d. renewal structure neither the construction of the invariant measure nor strict positivity of the velocity is available.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0040-absolutely-continuous-invariant-measure-for-the-environment-seen-from
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

body:

The direction 'invariant absolutely continuous probability measure for the environment process + transience in direction l implies ballisticity in direction l' is not open: it is Corollary 2.15 of the source (Drewitz-Ramirez, PDF pages 20-21), so A001's reduction of that direction to strict positivity of the velocity was solving a solved half.
